enonce_markdown: Which pair of features is found in mammals but in no other class of vertebrates?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To define a group, pick features that all its members have and that other groups lack.

### Solution

Hair (or fur) and mammary glands that produce milk are found only in mammals. A four-chambered heart and a constant body temperature are also found in birds, so they do not define mammals. The answer is **c**.

choix.texte: A four-chambered heart and a constant body temperature

enonce_markdown: Mammals are said to be *heterodont*. What does this mean?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Break the word up: hetero means different and dont means tooth.

### Solution

Mammals have incisors, canines, premolars and molars, each type with its own job (cutting, piercing, grinding). Therefore heterodont means teeth of different types, which is **b**.

choix.texte: They have no teeth at all
They have teeth of different shapes and sizes
They have teeth that are replaced all through life
They have only one row of identical teeth

enonce_markdown: Which muscular structure separating the thorax from the abdomen is found in mammals and helps in breathing?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Think about what moves when you breathe in: ribs and a muscular sheet below the lungs.

### Solution

The diaphragm flattens when it contracts, and this increases the volume of the chest so air flows in. Mammals have this structure; the ribs, trachea and pleural membranes are not a muscle sheet between the thorax and abdomen. The answer is **a**.

enonce_markdown: A bat can fly, but biologists place it among the mammals. Which observation best supports this classification?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The decisive feature is one that belongs to all mammals and to no other class, not the habit or the movement.

### Solution

A bat's wings do not decide its class, and a constant body temperature is shared with birds. Only milk produced by mammary glands is a mammalian feature, so the answer is **d**.

choix.texte: It is active during the night
It maintains a constant body temperature
The female feeds her young on milk from mammary glands

enonce_markdown:
The table shows features of four animals.

| Animal | Body covering | Young | Special features |
|---|---|---|---|
| W | Hair | Born alive and suckled | Pinna (external ear), diaphragm |
| X | Feathers | Hatch from eggs | Beak, wings |
| Y | Scales | Hatch from eggs | Body temperature changes with surroundings |
| Z | Almost hairless skin | Born alive and suckled | Lives in the sea, breathes with lungs |

State which animals are mammals and give **two** reasons for each choice. *(5 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Classify using the features that define the class, not the habitat.

### Solution

W and Z are mammals.

- W: it has hair, the young are born alive and fed on milk, and it has a diaphragm and an external ear.
- Z: although it lives in the sea and is almost hairless, it suckles its young (mammary glands) and breathes with lungs, as other mammals do.

X (feathers, eggs) is a bird and Y (scales, variable body temperature) is a reptile, so neither is a mammal.

enonce_markdown: A student claims that an animal is a mammal because it is warm-blooded and has a four-chambered heart. (i) Explain why this reasoning is not sufficient. (ii) State **two** features that would confirm the animal is a mammal. (iii) Explain how heterodont dentition helps mammals to feed. *(8 marks)*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A good defining feature must be true of every member of the group and untrue of related groups.

### Solution

(i) Birds are also warm-blooded and have a four-chambered heart, so these features do not separate mammals from birds.

(ii) Hair or fur on the body, and mammary glands that secrete milk to feed the young. A diaphragm or an external ear would also do.

(iii) Different teeth do different jobs: incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars crush and grind. Food is therefore broken into smaller pieces, with a larger surface for enzymes, which speeds up digestion.
